d: Watch this video as Firstpost explains how Burkinabè leader Ibrahim Traoré is pushing Burkina Faso to build its own technological and industrial future rather than relying on foreign powers—starting with the opening of the $66 million Académie Technologique du Faso (ATF) in Pabré, outside Ouagadougou. Built ahead of schedule by eleven Burkinabè companies over just more than ten months, the 60-hectare academy aims to serve as a homegrown counterpart to MIT, training an initial batch of 250 students in nuclear engineering, aeronautics, mining, and cybersecurity.
